```json
      "text": "I came from a school of one thousand people, I lived in a town of one thousand people for fifteen years; there's no reason that I should be in charge of an Athletics department, building maple leaf gardens."
    },
    {
      "start": 391.65,
      "end": 395.47,
      "text": "But I am the captain of my ship and the master of my fate."
    },
    {
      "start": 395.46,
      "end": 400.54,
      "text": "If I don't say it,  if I don't believe it, no one else will."
    },
    {
      "start": 400.54,
      "end": 403.16,
      "text": "How do you build self-confidence?"
    },
    {
      "start": 403.16,
      "end": 406.14,
      "text": "Get away from the people who will tear you down."
    },
    {
      "start": 406.14,
      "end": 407.5,
      "text": "There's enough of that."
    },
    {
      "start": 407.5,
      "end": 410.31,
      "text": "Muhammad Ali, I am the greatest!"
    },
    {
      "start": 410.31,
      "end": 413.03,
      "text": "There is no one better than me."
    },
    {
      "start": 413.02,
      "end": 417.07,
      "text": "There's a difference between hubris, and ego, and false pride."
    },
    {
      "start": 417.07,
      "end": 425.09,
      "text": "It's just reminding yourself in quiet silent moments, I put it down on a list, it's right beside my mirror, right?"
    },
    {
      "start": 425.09,
      "end": 427.13,
      "text": "about all the things that make me who I am."
    },
    {
      "start": 427.13,
      "end": 437.21,
      "text": "Because I make enough mistakes, and the newspapers will recognize it, and people around me will recognize it; and they'll tear me down, and pretty soon  I'll begin to believe it."
    },
    {
      "start": 437.21,
      "end": 440.58,
      "text": "There was a time when my confidence was really low."
    },
    {
      "start": 440.58,
      "end": 447.23,
      "text": "There was a time when I took this job when I came from Iowa, I don't know if I could do it."
    },
    {
      "start": 447.23,
      "end": 449.65,
      "text": "I had to bring out my self-confidence letter."
    },
    {
      "start": 449.65,
      "end": 452.63,
      "text": "A letter I wrote to myself when I was feeling good."
    },
    {
      "start": 452.63,
      "end": 456.13,
      "text": "Ivan, congratulations on getting your PhD before 40."
    },
    {
      "start": 456.13,
      "end": 460.58,
      "text": "Congra...I am 40, under."
    },
    {
      "start": 460.58,
      "end": 461.86,
      "text": "(Laughter)"
    },
    {
      "start": 461.86,
      "end": 464.04,
      "text": "Congratulations on winning a national championship."
    },
    {
      "start": 464.04,
      "end": 468.15,
      "text": "Good job on raising three good kids and marrying the right woman."
    },
    {
      "start": 468.15,
      "end": 471.79,
      "text": "I wrote a letter to myself, it was my own brag sheet."
    },
    {
      "start": 471.79,
      "end": 474.99,
      "text": "My own letter about the things I was proud of."
    },
    {
      "start": 474.99,
      "end": 486.16,
      "text": "Because there are moments, and we'll all experience them in our career, in our lives, in our job hunting,  in our relationships; when we are not feeling good about who, and what, and where we are."
    },
    {
      "start": 486.16,
      "end": 494.13,
      "text": "And I had to bring out that letter and read it time and time again, for a period of about two weeks, to weather me through that storm."
    },
    {
      "start": 494.5,
      "end": 495.78,
      "text": "It was important."
    },
    {
      "start": 496.65,
      "end": 499.79,
      "text": "Stop the self-talk, the negative self-talk."
    },
    {
      "start": 499.79,
      "end": 505.29,
      "text": "If you watch you'll see some athletes that have a little bandage, or a little brand around them."
    },
    {
      "start": 505.29,
      "end": 507.05,
      "text": "Lance Armstrong is a perfect one."
    },
    {
      "start": 507.05,
      "end": 509.29,
      "text": "What's his self-affirmation?"
    },
    {
      "start": 509.29,
      "end": 512.88,
      "text": "Livestrong isn't a brand, it was to remind him of who he was."
    },
    {
      "start": 512.88,
      "end": 514.04,
      "text": "Live strong."
    },
    {
      "start": 514.04,
      "end": 516.27,
      "text": "Then it became a brand."
    },
    {
      "start": 516.26,
      "end": 521.74,
      "text": "He would move that from one arm to the next arm, when doubt and fear came into his mind."
    },
    {
      "start": 521.74,
      "end": 523.82,
      "text": "Live strong, put it on there, let's go."
    },
    {
      "start": 524.68,
      "end": 527.63,
      "text": "We'll all have it, we place it."
    },
    {
      "start": 528.12,
      "end": 529.66,
      "text": "Two ways to build self-confidence."
    },
    {
      "start": 529.99,
      "end": 534.23,
      "text": "I'm worried about my time I'm gonna tell you of one way you can build self-confidence in others."
    },
    {
      "start": 534.23,
      "end": 542.99,
      "text": "We are coaches and educators, we are teachers, we are people who will create value in the world; and in doing that, we are critical by the nature of what we do."
    },
    {
      "start": 542.99,
      "end": 546.01,
      "text": "I am a coach,  I want you to score a goal."
    },
    {
      "start": 546.01,
      "end": 547.22,
      "text": "The ball went over high."
    },
    {
      "start": 547.22,
      "end": 547.73,
      "text": "\"Dang it!\""
    },
    {
      "start": 547.73,
      "end": 548.69,
      "text": "The ball went high!"
    },
    {
      "start": 548.69,
      "end": 550.56,
      "text": "\"Thank you coach, I know that."
    },
    {
      "start": 550.56,
      "end": 552.06,
      "text": "Feedback tells me that.\""
    },
    {
      "start": 552.06,
      "end": 553.01,
      "text": "So what do we do?"
    },
    {
      "start": 553.01,
      "end": 557.51,
      "text": "I need you to put your elbow here, I need you to put your knee over the ball, I need you to follow through."
    },
    {
      "start": 557.51,
      "end": 557.99,
      "text": "Boom."
    },
    {
      "start": 557.99,
      "end": 558.47,
      "text": "Land."
    },
    {
      "start": 558.47,
      "end": 559.05,
      "text": "Great."
    },
    {
      "start": 559.05,
      "end": 560.8,
      "text": "Notice, I never made it as a professional."
    },
    {
      "start": 560.8,
      "end": 561.79,
      "text": "(Laughter)"
    },
    {
      "start": 561.79,
      "end": 563.13,
      "text": "What can we do?"
    },
    {
      "start": 563.13,
      "end": 564.77,
      "text": "We fix mistakes."
    },
    {
      "start": 564.77,
      "end": 569.63,
      "text": "When I'm fixing that mistake: \"Johnny, this is terrible, you need to bend your knee, you need to do this, this.\""
    },
    {
      "start": 569.63,
      "end": 572.67,
      "text": "What have I done to Johnny's self-confidence?"
    },
    {
      "start": 572.67,
      "end": 575.01,
      "text": "Bend your knee, then do this, then do this."
    },
    {
      "start": 575.01,
      "end": 577.69,
      "text": "Next thing you know,  Johnny's crushed."
    },
    {
      "start": 578.66,
      "end": 583.56,
      "text": "Ignore what Johnny does wrong and find Bob or Sally  or Freda over here."
    },
    {
      "start": 583.56,
      "end": 590.12,
      "text": "Great goal Freda, I love how you kept your knee low, you followed through, and you landed like this."
    },
    {
      "start": 590.12,
      "end": 591.74,
      "text": "Great job!"
    },
    {
      "start": 591.74,
      "end": 592.95,
      "text": "Johnny: \"Oh?\""
    },
    {
      "start": 592.95,
      "end": 593.5,
      "text": "Great!"
    },
    {
      "start": 593.5,
      "end": 595.77,
      "text": "Johnny's not demoralized."
    },
    {
      "start": 595.77,
      "end": 600.33,
      "text": "His confidence isn't shot, and what I've done is, I've built up Freda's."
    },
    {
      "start": 600.33,
      "end": 603.9,
      "text": "Imagine how we could change the way we parented kids."
    },
    {
      "start": 603.9,
      "end": 606.56,
      "text": "Instead of: \"get that glass off the counter, what's wrong with you?\""
    },
    {
      "start": 606.56,
      "end": 607.72,
      "text": "(Laughter)"
    },
    {
      "start": 607.72,
      "end": 609.89,
      "text": "If we catch the mother, good."
    },
    {
      "start": 609.89,
      "end": 611.02,
      "text": "Great job!"
    },
    {
      "start": 611.02,
      "end": 612.15,
      "text": "Great job."
    },
    {
      "start": 612.14,
      "end": 614.4,
      "text": "Thank you Alice for taking your glass to the counter."
    },
    {
      "start": 614.4,
      "end": 616.66,
      "text": "It sounds simple but we forget about it."
    },
    {
      "start": 616.66,
      "end": 624.3,
      "text": "Or as educators, or as somebody as a team, if we manage to praise the positive behaviour that we wanted to reinforce."
    },
    {
      "start": 624.3,
      "end": 625.16,
      "text": "We forget it."
    },
    {
      "start": 625.16,
      "end": 626.49,
      "text": "It sounds so simple."
    },
    {
      "start": 626.49,
      "end": 629.14,
      "text": "Catch them when they're good."
    },
    {
      "start": 629.14,
      "end": 630.47,
      "text": "We forget it."
    },
    {
      "start": 630.47,
      "end": 631.69,
      "text": "It's simple."
    },
    {
      "start": 631.69,
      "end": 632.41,
      "text": "Here's what they did."
    },
    {
      "start": 632.41,
      "end": 633.95,
      "text": "There was a study in Kansas that did this."
    },
    {
      "start": 633.95,
      "end": 635.74,
      "text": "They did video, and we all do video."
    },
    {
      "start": 635.74,
      "end": 643.12,
      "text": "And we show the video of them doing the run of the play: \"Um, this goal happened because the basket wasn't protected, we didn't rotate here, right?"
    },
    {
      "start": 643.13,
      "end": 645.6,
      "text": "We needed to do this and then cover the slot.\""
    },
    {
      "start": 645.6,
      "end": 651.18,
      "text": "And, if that's the baseline, improvement of the Kansas State team went like this."
    },
    {
      "start": 651.81,
      "end": 657.54,
      "text": "Then, they said they ignored all of that and they just showed them the times they did it right."
    },
    {
      "start": 657.54,
      "end": 659.32,
      "text": "The times they did it perfect."
    },
    {
      "start": 659.32,
      "end": 664.79,
      "text": "That presented no goals, spoke to the same points, improvement went like that."
    },
    {
      "start": 664.78,
      "end": 669.42,
      "text": "It changed and revolutionized the way we as coaches interact with our student athletes."
    },
    {
      "start": 669.42,
      "end": 675.28,
      "text": "We can apply that to the business world, we can apply that to our student group works, we can apply that to our management teams."
    },
    {
      "start": 675.28,
      "end": 679.62,
      "text": "Easily: catch them when they are good."
    },
    {
      "start": 679.62,
      "end": 681.61,
      "text": "Last and certainly not least."
    },
    {
      "start": 681.61,
      "end": 684.16,
      "text": "My son is really good at this."
    },
    {
      "start": 684.16,
      "end": 689.64,
      "text": "Self-confident people interpret feedback the way they choose to."
    },
    {
      "start": 689.64,
      "end": 694.46,
      "text": "I ask my son who is by the far a terrible, terrible athlete, gets it from his dad."
    },
    {
      "start": 694.46,
      "end": 695.79,
      "text": "(Laughter)"
    },
    {
      "start": 695.8,
      "end": 696.99,
      "text": "The game's..."
    },
    {
      "start": 696.99,
      "end": 697.97,
      "text": "How's the game?"
    },
    {
      "start": 697.98,
      "end": 698.54,
      "text": "Oh great!"
    },
    {
      "start": 698.54,
      "end": 701.01,
      "text": "I scored three goals, I got two assists."
    },
    {
      "start": 701.0,
      "end": 703.6,
      "text": "I'm like: \"I did not see him  touch the puck!\""
    },
    {
      "start": 703.61,
      "end": 708.01,
      "text": "But he has his own perception of how he did!"
    },
    {
      "start": 708.01,
      "end": 709.27,
      "text": "(Laughter)"
    },
    {
      "start": 709.27,
      "end": 710.57,
      "text": "I love it!"
    },
    {
      "start": 710.56,
      "end": 711.46,
      "text": "(Laughter)"
    },
    {
      "start": 711.46,
      "end": 711.93,
      "text": "Right?"
    },
    {
      "start": 711.93,
      "end": 713.73,
      "text": "I'm the...I'm that guy!"
    },
    {
      "start": 713.73,
      "end": 718.12,
      "text": "I'm like: \"I remember when I was taking when I met my wife,  it was in the commons."
    },
    {
      "start": 718.12,
      "end": 720.25,
      "text": "\"Paulie, would you like  to go to the movies?"
    },
    {
      "start": 720.25,
      "end": 720.65,
      "text": "Ladies?"
    },
    {
      "start": 720.65,
      "end": 722.0,
      "text": "Tingly, tingly, tingle.\""
    },
    {
      "start": 722.0,
      "end": 723.86,
      "text": "(Laughter)"
    },
    {
      "start": 724.8,
      "end": 730.07,
      "text": "And she goes: \"Ah, no.\" I asked her again."
    },
    {
      "start": 730.08,
      "end": 732.36,
      "text": "Cause I think that she just hasn't seen me in the right light."
    },
    {
      "start": 732.36,
      "end": 733.39,
      "text": "(Laughter)"
    },
    {
      "start": 733.39,
      "end": 735.1,
      "text": "Maybe, that's not the wrong shirt on."
    },
    {
      "start": 735.1,
      "end": 735.59,
      "text": "Right?"
    },
    {
      "start": 735.59,
      "end": 738.6,
      "text": "Cause I'm interpreting that the way I want to interpret it."
    },
    {
      "start": 738.6,
      "end": 740.68,
      "text": "Finally I asked her out again."
    },
    {
      "start": 740.68,
      "end": 742.34,
      "text": "She gave me this one comment, right?"
    },
    {
      "start": 742.34,
      "end": 743.73,
      "text": "Or, she sent it to her friend."
    },
    {
      "start": 743.73,
      "end": 745.01,
      "text": "Cause that's the way  you did it back then."
    },
    {
      "start": 745.01,
      "end": 752.99,
      "text": "\"She wouldn't date you unless there was the last person on Earth, hell was freezing over, there was a small chance we had to save the planet Earth."
    },
    {
      "start": 752.99,
      "end": 754.69,
      "text": "Some people, it's like,  there's no chance."
    },
    {
      "start": 754.69,
      "end": 756.68,
      "text": "I'm like: \"You're saying there's a chance.\""
    },
    {
      "start": 756.68,
      "end": 758.03,
      "text": "(Laughter)"
    },
    {
      "start": 758.02,
      "end": 759.49,
      "text": "Right?"
    },
    {
      "start": 759.49,
      "end": 762.42,
      "text": "Because that's how  I'm gonna interpret it."
    },
    {
      "start": 762.42,
      "end": 769.52,
      "text": "If I could give you one thing to take from this, it is: no one will believe in you unless you do."
    },
    {
      "start": 769.52,
      "end": 780.47,
      "text": "Listen to the words of that video, here's to the crazy ones, the misfits, the rebels, the troublemakers, the round pegs in the square holes."
    },
    {
      "start": 780.46,
      "end": 783.03,
      "text": "We're supposed to be different, folks."
    },
    {
      "start": 783.03,
      "end": 787.33,
      "text": "And when people look at us, believe in yourself."
    },
    {
      "start": 787.33,
      "end": 788.25,
      "text": "Thank you."
    },
    {
      "start": 788.25,
      "end": 792.25,
      "text": "(Applause)"
    }
  ],
  "Sxxw3qtb3_g": [
    {
      "start": 0.08,
      "end": 10.88,
      "text": "If you're learning to code, it means you probably have a billion-dollar startup idea in your head, but before you can execute that idea, you'll need to choose a tech stack, and you better choose wisely."
    },
    {
      "start": 9.4,
      "end": 16.8,
      "text": "Because it's a real pain in the ass if you decide to change it later, every app is actually just a technology sandwich."
    },
    {
      "start": 14.96,
      "end": 24.08,
      "text": "And in today's video, I will teach you how to make a sandwich; we'll look at popular stacks like LAMP, MEAN, MEAN, and so on."
    },
    {
      "start": 21.28,
      "end": 29.56,
      "text": "Then we'll architect our own tech stack from scratch and look at the decision-making process for each layer in the stack."
    },
    {
      "start": 27.6,
      "end": 33.2,
      "text": "By the end of the video, you'll know how to over-engineer a website like a true professional."
    },
    {
      "start": 33.2,
      "end": 39.96,
      "text": "If you're new here, like and subscribe, and let me know what kind of tech stack you're using in the comments."
    },
    {
      "start": 37.84,
      "end": 47.88,
      "text": "The OG tech stack is LAMP, which came about in the late '90s and stands for Linux, Apache, MySQL, and PHP."
    },
    {
      "start": 45.72,
      "end": 53.48,
      "text": "Building a web application in the '90s was a lot more complicated and typically required expensive commercial software."
    },
    {
      "start": 51.92,
      "end": 57.4,
      "text": "LAMP was a free and open-source stack that eventually led to web frameworks like WordPress and Joomla."
    },
    {
      "start": 55.28,
      "end": 64.4,
      "text": "In modern times, building a web application is much easier, but tech stacks have become far more complicated because there are so many different companies selling shovels in the startup gold rush."
    },
    {
      "start": 62.8,
      "end": 70.24,
      "text": "That begs the question, what is a tech stack exactly?"
    },
    {
      "start": 68.48,
      "end": 73.8,
      "text": "There's no official definition, but I would break it down into three parts."
    },
    {
      "start": 72.0,
      "end": 82.0,
      "text": "First, you have the front-end layer, which includes the tools required to build a user interface for the end user on the web; that likely means a JavaScript framework, or for mobile, it might be iOS, Android, or a cross-platform tool like Flutter."
    },
    {
      "start": 79.52,
      "end": 90.24,
      "text": "At the other end, we have the back-end layer, which includes a server-side runtime like Node.js or Python, along with a database to store user-generated data."
    },
    {
      "start": 87.56,
      "end": 97.88,
      "text": "In addition, you'll likely purchase this infrastructure from a big cloud provider, and they'll try to lock you in."
    },
    {
      "start": 96.24,
      "end": 126.68,
      "text": "Cloud providers will try to lock you in, so I would consider them as part of your tech stack as well."
    },
    {
      "start": 125.2,
      "end": 140.68,
      "text": "Now let's take a look at some common tech stacks that you've probably heard of, starting with MEAN, which stands for MongoDB, Express, Angular, and Node."
    },
    {
      "start": 139.28,
      "end": 145.72,
      "text": "The reason this stack got so popular is because it has a catchy acronym."
    },
    {
      "start": 143.64,
      "end": 156.76,
      "text": "It's important to make that acronym pop because it will automatically make other people in the tech industry think you know what you're doing."
    },
    {
      "start": 155.32,
      "end": 164.64,
      "text": "Others have realized this with the MEAN stack, and there are variations like MERN and MEAN, which use React and Vue respectively."
    },
    {
      "start": 162.52,
      "end": 170.44,
      "text": "The reality though is that these acronyms don't accurately capture everything you really need in a tech stack."
    },
    {
      "start": 169.0,
      "end": 177.6,
      "text": "If you want to see what other successful companies are using in their stacks, there's a website called Stackshare.io."
    },
    {
      "start": 175.92,
      "end": 188.88,
      "text": "Let's go ahead and build our own from scratch, but the first time around, let's use the hottest of the hot technologies at every single point regardless of cost or complexity."
    },
    {
      "start": 187.44,
      "end": 192.92,
      "text": "Don't worry, by the end of the video, we'll come back and simplify things in a much more practical way."
    },
    {
      "start": 190.68,
      "end": 196.88,
      "text": "This requires user authentication to store user-generated data."
    },
    {
      "start": 194.84,
      "end": 200.48,
      "text": "Let's start by architecting the front end layer."
    },
    {
      "start": 198.64,
      "end": 205.4,
      "text": "The very first question you need to ask is where will my customers be consuming the application?"
    },
    {
      "start": 202.44,
      "end": 209.8,
      "text": "Is it the web, iOS, Android, desktop, IoT, or something else?"
    },
    {
      "start": 208.08,
      "end": 213.56,
      "text": "For this app, we'll assume that our customers are primarily on the web, but we might also want to build a mobile app in the future."
    },
    {
      "start": 211.76,
      "end": 216.92,
      "text": "When targeting the web, the programming language in your front-end layer will almost always be JavaScript."
    },
    {
      "start": 215.28,
      "end": 220.36,
      "text": "There are tools that can help you avoid JavaScript if you really want to."
    },
    {
      "start": 218.76,
      "end": 223.52,
      "text": "If your goal is to build a killer web app, I would highly recommend embracing JavaScript."
    },
    {
      "start": 221.96,
      "end": 227.08,
      "text": "But we need this app to scale, so we're not just going to use vanilla JavaScript."
    },
    {
      "start": 225.56,
      "end": 230.92,
      "text": "Instead, TypeScript adds a type system on top of JavaScript, which might help us catch bugs earlier and deliver more reliable code."
    },
    {
      "start": 228.88,
      "end": 234.48,
      "text": "The next thing we need is a UI framework."
    },
    {
      "start": 232.64,
      "end": 237.92,
      "text": "Trying to build a complex UI with vanilla JavaScript is very painful."
    },
    {
      "start": 236.0,
      "end": 242.0,
      "text": "There are too many options to even analyze."
    },
    {
      "start": 240.0,
      "end": 245.56,
      "text": "I'm choosing React for this app, not because it's the best or the fastest, but because it's the most popular."
    },
    {
      "start": 243.8,
      "end": 249.48,
      "text": "Sadly, many decisions end up being a popularity contest."
    },
    {
      "start": 247.4,
      "end": 253.92,
      "text": "As much as I wanted to choose Svelte, I know that choosing React will give me a much larger pool of developers to hire in the future."
    },
    {
      "start": 251.88,
      "end": 257.0,
      "text": "On top of that, I can more easily add React Native to my stack to build a mobile app."
    },
    {
      "start": 255.4,
      "end": 260.92,
      "text": "But React on its own is still not enough for our web application."
    },
    {
      "start": 258.92,
      "end": 265.16,
      "text": "We heard on the street that we'll need a state management solution if our app has any hope to scale."
    },
    {
      "start": 263.04,
      "end": 268.2,
      "text": "There are dozens of different state management libraries for React alone."
    },
    {
      "start": 266.8,
      "end": 272.0,
      "text": "We'll choose the most popular option that everybody also hates the most, Redux."
    },
    {
      "start": 270.08,
      "end": 275.4,
      "text": "It allows us to write a lot more boilerplate code, which is awesome."
    },
    {
      "start": 273.56,
      "end": 279.28,
      "text": "We all know that more code leads to better quality apps."
    },
    {
      "start": 277.16,
      "end": 286.88,
      "text": "Redux hates the most; it allows us to write a lot more boilerplate code, which is awesome because we all know that more code leads to better quality apps."
    },
    {
      "start": 285.28,
      "end": 294.12,
      "text": "Another glaring problem with our tech stack is that it's currently using vanilla CSS; it's basically impossible to make CSS look good on its own."
    },
    {
      "start": 292.28,
      "end": 303.24,
      "text": "So we're going to bring in Tailwind; that'll give us a bunch of pre-built utility classes to style things quickly in exchange for some crazy looking HTML."
    },
    {
      "start": 300.32,
      "end": 307.12,
      "text": "We're also going to want a CSS pre-processor like SAS; just like TypeScript, it provides some extra syntax to help us write code more efficiently."
    },
    {
      "start": 305.0,
      "end": 311.36,
      "text": "We're also going to need PostCSS to purge any unused styles from our codebase and prepare our CSS for production."
    },
    {
      "start": 315.16,
      "end": 320.28,
      "text": "Now at this point, we have almost everything we need to build the front end; the only thing we're missing is a module bundler."
    },
    {
      "start": 318.36,
      "end": 326.0,
      "text": "A module bundler takes all of our raw JavaScript files and combines them into a single bundle that can be used in the browser."
    },
    {
      "start": 324.2,
      "end": 329.4,
      "text": "There are many options to choose from, and they're notoriously frustrating to configure."
    },
    {
      "start": 327.6,
      "end": 332.84,
      "text": "I'm going with Webpack, which is the most popular option today; that'll give us almost everything we need for the front end stack."
    },
    {
      "start": 333.96,
      "end": 339.28,
      "text": "Now it's time to switch gears to the hard part: the back end."
    },
    {
      "start": 337.8,
      "end": 345.96,
      "text": "The most important decision you'll make here is the database for your user-generated data; a good option for us might be a NoSQL document database like MongoDB or Firestore."
    },
    {
      "start": 343.12,
      "end": 352.16,
      "text": "They're easy to learn, inexpensive, and can scale to practically any workload."
    },
    {
      "start": 350.16,
      "end": 355.92,
      "text": "But they sometimes struggle to model certain types of relationships, especially things like a social graph that we might want for our MySpace clone."
    },
    {
      "start": 358.12,
      "end": 366.4,
      "text": "The most popular database option out there is the relational database, like MySQL, PostgreSQL, and many other options."
    },
    {
      "start": 364.88,
      "end": 369.88,
      "text": "These databases are great at handling relationships, but they're not quite as flexible to changing requirements and generally more expensive to operate."
    },
    {
      "start": 376.0,
      "end": 379.84,
      "text": "Now that we've chosen our database, we find an article on the web that says it's not going to be fast enough at scale."
    },
    {
      "start": 383.68,
      "end": 392.92,
      "text": "To address this, we're going to add a second database to our stack called Redis, which is often used as a cache because it stores all your data in memory, as opposed to the disk, which is much faster to read from."
    },
    {
      "start": 394.96,
      "end": 400.92,
      "text": "In order to put these databases to work, we need a server-side runtime where we can write code to access data and then send it back to the front end."
    },
    {
      "start": 417.84,
      "end": 425.96,
      "text": "As a JavaScript developer, I'm going to go with Node.js as my runtime and then use a framework called Nest to handle the server-side web application stuff."
    },
    {
      "start": 431.64,
      "end": 444.32,
      "text": "We're going to bring in an object relational mapper like TypeORM, so that gives us a runtime for writing and executing code on a server."
    },
    {
      "start": 442.08,
      "end": 448.32,
      "text": "We also need a web server like Nginx or Apache, so let's throw one of those on the stack as well."
    },
    {
      "start": 452.16,
      "end": 457.96,
      "text": "Before we can do that, we need to standardize the environment for our code by containerizing it with Docker."
    },
    {
      "start": 457.96,
      "end": 463.16,
      "text": "This creates a standard Linux environment that we can then use to deploy our code to any Cloud server."
    },
    {
      "start": 461.76,
      "end": 477.68,
      "text": "As our app scales, we'll need to orchestrate multiple containers, so we're going to bring in Kubernetes."
    },
    {
      "start": 475.8,
      "end": 488.12,
      "text": "Then we'll need to choose one or more cloud providers to host all this infrastructure; let's go with Amazon Web Services to give us the most complicated user experience."
    },
    {
      "start": 491.64,
      "end": 504.24,
      "text": "The reason we want to host our source code in the cloud is to set up a continuous integration pipeline, and we can add GitHub Actions to the stack to automatically test and redeploy our code anytime we push an update to the repository."
    },
    {
      "start": 502.28,
      "end": 515.6,
      "text": "That gives us a solid backend, but there are many things our app needs to do that are just too complicated to handle from scratch; one of those things is building an API for our front end and backend to communicate."
    },
    {
      "start": 513.8,
      "end": 527.8,
      "text": "We heard on the internet that GraphQL is awesome, so we're going to add it to the stack along with a library called Apollo, which will provide code on both our front end and back end to help us build a GraphQL API that allows the front end to securely communicate with the backend."
    },
    {
      "start": 529.08,
      "end": 536.92,
      "text": "Another thing we're not going to want to do is deal with payments, so for that, we're going to bring in Stripe, which provides SDKs for both the server and front end to collect payments."
    },
    {
      "start": 536.92,
      "end": 544.4,
      "text": "We also don't want to deal with user authentication, so we'll bring in Zero to handle that, and we also don't want dudes uploading dick pics to our platform."
    },
    {
      "start": 542.48,
      "end": 549.72,
      "text": "So we'll bring in Amazon Recognition with its deep learning dick detection capabilities."
    },
    {
      "start": 548.12,
      "end": 556.08,
      "text": "We also have no idea how to send text messages to our users, so we'll bring in Twilio to help us with that."
    },
    {
      "start": 553.64,
      "end": 559.4,
      "text": "I could keep going here, but you get the idea; we use APIs to help us for the things that are too hard to do."
    },
    {
      "start": 557.64,
      "end": 564.28,
      "text": "On our own at this point, we have a nearly complete text stack, but it's likely way more complicated than it needs to be."
    },
    {
      "start": 562.76,
      "end": 569.96,
      "text": "It's important to keep in mind that your end users don't care and will never know what technology you use to build the application."
    },
    {
      "start": 568.32,
      "end": 574.6,
      "text": "They just want to have a good experience, and if you don't build a good experience at first, you'll never get to the point where you actually need something like Kubernetes."
    },
    {
      "start": 576.6,
      "end": 581.84,
      "text": "Let's go ahead and throw this entire text stack in the garbage and start from a plain HTML file."
    },
    {
      "start": 579.48,
      "end": 587.16,
      "text": "Now our web app does need to be interactive, so we need some kind of JavaScript framework."
    },
    {
      "start": 585.36,
      "end": 592.88,
      "text": "Instead of something big and heavy, let's throw in a new option called Petite View, which has a syntax that's compatible with Vue.js."
    },
    {
      "start": 591.08,
      "end": 596.08,
      "text": "Many developers out there already know it, and we can drop it in with a script tag."
    },
    {
      "start": 594.6,
      "end": 600.44,
      "text": "So we're not even going to need a module bundle like Webpack."
    },
    {
      "start": 598.04,
      "end": 607.16,
      "text": "When it comes to CSS, we'll throw in Bootstrap, which is a little more cookie cutter than something like Tailwind, but is probably the quickest way to get to a decent looking UI."
    },
    {
      "start": 605.28,
      "end": 612.24,
      "text": "If we decide we need a mobile app, we're going to bring in Ionic to wrap our application in a web view, allowing us to quickly ship it off to iOS and Android."
    },
    {
      "start": 610.56,
      "end": 615.96,
      "text": "That takes care of our front end stack."
    },
    {
      "start": 613.92,
      "end": 623.92,
      "text": "To simplify the back end, we'll bring in Firebase, which gives us a document database that can scale without any need for a backend server."
    },
    {
      "start": 622.04,
      "end": 629.48,
      "text": "It also handles user authentication, and we can include it in the application by simply adding a script tag to the document."
    },
    {
      "start": 627.84,
      "end": 642.88,
      "text": "Now we still might want to write some server side code, in which case we can use Firebase Cloud Functions, which is a serverless option that allows us to write code in Node.js or Python or Go if you prefer."
    },
    {
      "start": 640.88,
      "end": 646.28,
      "text": "It scales automatically without ever having to worry about Docker, Kubernetes, or Terraform."
    },
    {
      "start": 647.92,
      "end": 656.56,
      "text": "We're just not going to worry about it unless you find yourself testing and redeploying your app every day; it's probably just a waste of time."
    },
    {
      "start": 654.8,
      "end": 662.6,
      "text": "We can also get rid of GraphQL because it's more well suited for complex apps that have multi APIs to stitch together."
    },
    {
      "start": 661.0,
      "end": 667.2,
      "text": "And that leaves us with the petite Fire stack, which is quite possibly the easiest way to build a full stack web application."
    },
    {
      "start": 665.92,
      "end": 670.36,
      "text": "I'm going to go ahead and wrap things up there, but if you want to learn more about building full stack web applications with Firebase using multiple different front end frameworks, check out Fireship Pro to get access to my full courses."
    },
    {
      "start": 675.52,
      "end": 681.8,
      "text": "Thanks for watching, and I will see you in the next one."
    }
  ],
  "erEgovG9WBs": [
    {
      "start": 0.04,
      "end": 21.28,
      "text": "Web development is the best job in the world; you build on a platform with nearly 5 billion daily active users, all connected together like the neurons of a global super intelligent brain."
    },
    {
      "start": 19.72,
      "end": 31.96,
      "text": "If you want to get into it, you're going to need to know some stuff, like a lot of stuff in web development 101; we'll take a look at 10 different concepts that you'll need to know when building full stack web apps."
    },
    {
      "start": 30.16,
      "end": 36.0,
      "text": "This is the Internet; it's a network of billions of machines connected together."
    },
    {
      "start": 41.32,
      "end": 53.56,
      "text": "Allison, can you explain what the internet is? It was officially born on January 1st, 1983, thanks to the establishment of the Internet Protocol Suite, which standardized the way these computers communicate."
    },
    {
      "start": 51.76,
      "end": 61.4,
      "text": "The Internet Protocol is used to identify different computers on the network by assigning each one of them a unique IP address; these computers can then send data back and forth with the transmission control protocol."
    },
    {
      "start": 59.32,
      "end": 73.48,
      "text": "It breaks data into a bunch of small packets, kind of like puzzle pieces, then sends them through a bunch of physical components like fiber optic cables and modems before they're put back together by the receiving computer."
    },
    {
      "start": 71.56,
      "end": 77.6,
      "text": "You can think of the internet as hardware, but the internet is not the same thing as the web."
    },
    {
      "start": 75.28,
      "end": 84.88,
      "text": "The worldwide web is like software that sits on top of the internet, where people can access web pages with the hypertext transfer protocol."
    },
    {
      "start": 83.24,
      "end": 95.64,
      "text": "What's special about it is that it gives every page of content a uniform resource locator or URL; humans typically use a tool called a web browser to access a URL where it can be rendered visually."
    },
    {
      "start": 93.72,
      "end": 97.32,
      "text": "On their screen, the browser is called."
    },
    {
      "start": 95.64,
      "end": 103.56,
      "text": "The client consumes information, but on the other end of that URL, there's another computer called a server."
    },
    {
      "start": 101.28,
      "end": 107.2,
      "text": "It received an HTTP request from the client, then sent a response."
    },
    {
      "start": 105.32,
      "end": 109.64,
      "text": "These are called HTTP messages, but more on that later."
    },
    {
      "start": 109.64,
      "end": 113.6,
      "text": "What's interesting is that every web page has a unique domain name."
    },
    {
      "start": 111.32,
      "end": 118.64,
      "text": "A domain name can be registered by anyone via a registrar."
    },
    {
      "start": 118.64,
      "end": 126.52,
      "text": "Whose accredited by ICANN, a nonprofit responsible for overseeing name spaces on the internet."
    },
    {
      "start": 126.52,
      "end": 129.84,
      "text": "When you navigate to a domain in a browser, it gets routed through the domain name system."
    },
    {
      "start": 129.84,
      "end": 133.44,
      "text": "That maps these names to an actual IP address on a server somewhere."
    },
    {
      "start": 131.88,
      "end": 135.4,
      "text": "DNS is like the phone book of the internet."
    },
    {
      "start": 133.44,
      "end": 137.12,
      "text": "Now, when you look at a web page, the actual content you see is represented by hypertext markup language."
    },
    {
      "start": 135.4,
      "end": 141.48,
      "text": "Most browsers have Dev tools where you can inspect the structure of the HTML at any time."
    },
    {
      "start": 143.6,
      "end": 147.64,
      "text": "To build your own web page, you'll want a text editor like VS Code."
    },
    {
      "start": 147.64,
      "end": 152.44,
      "text": "An HTML document is just a collection of elements."
    },
    {
      "start": 150.44,
      "end": 156.36,
      "text": "Where an element is an opening and closing tag with some content in the middle, like a paragraph and heading."
    },
    {
      "start": 156.36,
      "end": 160.56,
      "text": "It also has elements that handle user input."
    },
    {
      "start": 158.48,
      "end": 164.28,
      "text": "Like the select and input elements, which are used to build forms."
    },
    {
      "start": 162.6,
      "end": 166.48,
      "text": "In addition, elements can have one or more attributes to change their behavior."
    },
    {
      "start": 164.28,
      "end": 170.16,
      "text": "For example, an input can have a type like text or number."
    },
    {
      "start": 170.16,
      "end": 173.72,
      "text": "Which the browser will render differently to collect the appropriate value."
    },
    {
      "start": 173.72,
      "end": 180.88,
      "text": "But the element that puts the hypertext in HTML is the \"a\" tag or anchor."
    },
    {
      "start": 178.96,
      "end": 183.08,
      "text": "It's a link that allows one page to navigate to a different page based on its URL."
    },
    {
      "start": 180.88,
      "end": 184.96,
      "text": "These elements are nested together in a hierarchy to form the document object model or DOM."
    },
    {
      "start": 184.96,
      "end": 189.16,
      "text": "From the root element, a web page is split into two parts."
    },
    {
      "start": 189.16,
      "end": 195.08,
      "text": "The head contains invisible content like metadata and a title."
    },
    {
      "start": 193.32,
      "end": 197.04,
      "text": "Then we have the body for the main content."
    },
    {
      "start": 197.04,
      "end": 214.6,
      "text": "The reason we wrap everything in tags is to give browsers and bots hints about the semantic meaning of the web page; this allows search engines to display results properly and also helps with accessibility for devices like screen readers that allow anybody, regardless of disability, to enjoy the content."
    },
    {
      "start": 214.6,
      "end": 220.28,
      "text": "Smash that like button and subscribe; one of the most common elements you'll come across is div or division to define a section of the web page."
    },
    {
      "start": 220.28,
      "end": 229.64,
      "text": "A div might not seem to do anything and currently produces this plain black and white website that begs the question, how do we make this website look cool?"
    },
    {
      "start": 229.64,
      "end": 237.88,
      "text": "The second language you'll need to learn as a web developer is cascading stylesheets, or CSS, which allows you to change the appearance of the HTML elements."
    },
    {
      "start": 237.88,
      "end": 248.88,
      "text": "One way to accomplish that is with an inline style using the style attribute on an element; the style itself contains a collection of properties and values that change the appearance of the element."
    },
    {
      "start": 247.36,
      "end": 254.76,
      "text": "For example, we might make the background color black and the text color red; what we've created here is an inline style that will only be applied to this one element."
    },
    {
      "start": 254.76,
      "end": 264.28,
      "text": "However, CSS cascades, which means it can be applied to multiple elements at the same time, providing better code reusability."
    },
    {
      "start": 262.04,
      "end": 272.12,
      "text": "Another option is to move our code into a style tag, but to make the code work, we'll first need to define a selector so it knows which elements to target."
    },
    {
      "start": 270.44,
      "end": 280.0,
      "text": "A selector, for example, can target all of the paragraph elements on the page, but that's too broad; we can be more granular by defining a class that style can then be applied to one or more elements with the class attribute."
    },
    {
      "start": 283.4,
      "end": 291.2,
      "text": "What's interesting though is that we now have classes that apply different styles to the same element; CSS contains a bunch of specificity rules that determine which styles are relevant to an element in a way that's self-evident and elegant."
    },
    {
      "start": 293.2,
      "end": 300.24,
      "text": "We don't use style tags but instead use an external style sheet which is linked to the web page in the head of the document."
    },
    {
      "start": 300.24,
      "end": 306.04,
      "text": "By far the most difficult thing to learn is layout and positioning."
    },
    {
      "start": 303.88,
      "end": 311.8,
      "text": "Think of every element like a box; the outside of that box is wrapped with padding, border, and margin."
    },
    {
      "start": 311.8,
      "end": 318.04,
      "text": "Some elements like heading have a display of block by default, which means they take up all available horizontal space."
    },
    {
      "start": 318.04,
      "end": 323.4,
      "text": "Other elements like image are displayed inline, which means they can line up horizontally side by side."
    },
    {
      "start": 323.4,
      "end": 328.92,
      "text": "The problem is that the default position is usually not desirable."
    },
    {
      "start": 331.08,
      "end": 337.08,
      "text": "Relative positioning allows an element to move a certain number of pixels from its normal position."
    },
    {
      "start": 337.08,
      "end": 342.2,
      "text": "Absolute positioning is similar but the position values are relative to its nearest ancestor."
    },
    {
      "start": 340.48,
      "end": 345.84,
      "text": "Then we have fixed positioning, which will keep an element on the screen even as the user scrolls away from it."
    },
    {
      "start": 349.28,
      "end": 355.12,
      "text": "One of the biggest challenges web developers face is creating responsive layouts."
    },
    {
      "start": 353.4,
      "end": 358.8,
      "text": "Users can access your web page from all kinds of different screens, and it should look good on all of them."
    },
    {
      "start": 356.56,
      "end": 364.16,
      "text": "CSS provides a bunch of different tools to help make this happen, one of which is Media queries."
    },
    {
      "start": 362.48,
      "end": 369.2,
      "text": "A media query allows you to get information about the device that's rendering the web page and apply different styles accordingly."
    },
    {
      "start": 369.2,
      "end": 375.28,
      "text": "But more importantly, it provides layout tools like flexbox."
    },
    {
      "start": 373.32,
      "end": 379.72,
      "text": "Applying display Flex allows the parent to control the flow of the children to easily create rows and columns for more complex layouts."
    },
    {
      "start": 379.72,
      "end": 385.92,
      "text": "Display grid can be used to control multiple rows and columns at the same time."
    },
    {
      "start": 383.68,
      "end": 389.96,
      "text": "CSS is usually not considered a Turing complete programming language on its own."
    },
    {
      "start": 387.8,
      "end": 393.6,
      "text": "However, it does have mechanisms like calc to perform mathematical operations."
    },
    {
      "start": 392.24,
      "end": 398.0,
      "text": "Custom properties which are like variables that you can reuse in multiple places."
    },
    {
      "start": 395.76,
      "end": 401.56,
      "text": "Vanilla CSS is rarely enough."
    },
    {
      "start": 399.52,
      "end": 404.8,
      "text": "Many developers choose to extend it with tools like Sass that add additional programmatic features on top."
    },
    {
      "start": 403.36,
      "end": 408.56,
      "text": "That brings us to the third language you'll need to know as a web developer, JavaScript."
    },
    {
      "start": 406.32,
      "end": 411.96,
      "text": "Technically, you don't need JavaScript to build a website."
    },
    {
      "start": 410.4,
      "end": 415.32,
      "text": "However, most developers choose to use it to make the user interface more interactive."
    },
    {
      "start": 413.32,
      "end": 419.16,
      "text": "To run JavaScript code on a web page, open up a script tag then write some JavaScript code inside of it."
    },
    {
      "start": 417.56,
      "end": 422.68,
      "text": "The browser interprets the HTML from top to bottom and runs this code when it encounters it in the DOM."
    },
    {
      "start": 421.2,
      "end": 426.72,
      "text": "In most cases, JavaScript is written in a separate file then referenced as the source on the script tag."
    },
    {
      "start": 424.76,
      "end": 430.0,
      "text": "Usually, it's preferred that this code runs after the DOM content has loaded, which can be accomplished with the defer attribute."
    },
    {
      "start": 433.48,
      "end": 439.52,
      "text": "JS is a big, complicated programming language which is more formally known as ECMAScript."
    },
    {
      "start": 437.36,
      "end": 442.88,
      "text": "It is standardized in all major browsers."
    },
    {
      "start": 441.72,
      "end": 446.68,
      "text": "There are several different ways to declare a variable."
    },
    {
      "start": 444.72,
      "end": 450.68,
      "text": "A variable that might be reassigned in the future uses the let keyword."
    },
    {
      "start": 448.44,
      "end": 454.0,
      "text": "While a variable that can't be reassigned uses const."
    },
    {
      "start": 452.28,
      "end": 457.72,
      "text": "It's a dynamically typed language which means no type annotations are necessary."
    },
    {
      "start": 455.92,
      "end": 461.16,
      "text": "That's not always ideal, so many developers choose TypeScript as an alternative to add static typing on top of JavaScript."
    },
    {
      "start": 459.88,
      "end": 464.88,
      "text": "One of the most common reasons you would use JavaScript in the first place is to handle events."
    },
    {
      "start": 463.12,
      "end": 468.8,
      "text": "Whenever the user does something on a web page, the browser emits an event that you can listen to."
    },
    {
      "start": 466.76,
      "end": 473.04,
      "text": "Like a click, mouse move, form input change, and so on."
    },
    {
      "start": 471.12,
      "end": 477.12,
      "text": "We can tap into these events using browser APIs like document."
    },
    {
      "start": 475.56,
      "end": 482.68,
      "text": "which in this case provides a method called query selector that allows us to grab an element El with a CSS selector."
    },
    {
      "start": 481.24,
      "end": 486.48,
      "text": "once we have that element set as a variable we can then assign an event listener to it."
    },
    {
      "start": 484.48,
      "end": 492.08,
      "text": "an event listener is a function that will be called or re-executed anytime the button is clicked."
    },
    {
      "start": 490.32,
      "end": 496.56,
      "text": "the language has a variety of built-in data structures like an array to represent a collection of values."
    },
    {
      "start": 494.16,
      "end": 500.16,
      "text": "but the most fundamental data structure is the object also commonly called a dictionary or hashmap."
    },
    {
      "start": 498.32,
      "end": 505.92,
      "text": "anything that's not a primitive type like a string or number inherits its base functionality from the object class."
    },
    {
      "start": 503.92,
      "end": 511.92,
      "text": "it relies on a technique called prototypal inheritance."
    },
    {
      "start": 510.16,
      "end": 517.84,
      "text": "where an object can be cloned multiple times to create a chain of ancestors where the child inherits the properties and methods of its ancestors."
    },
    {
      "start": 515.88,
      "end": 521.0,
      "text": "this is different from class-based inheritance."
    },
    {
      "start": 519.6,
      "end": 525.52,
      "text": "which is kind of confusing because JavaScript also supports classes."
    },
    {
      "start": 523.48,
      "end": 529.12,
      "text": "however, these classes are just syntactic sugar for prototypal inheritance."
    },
    {
      "start": 527.52,
      "end": 534.08,
      "text": "but now we're getting a little too low level."
    },
    {
      "start": 532.04,
      "end": 539.76,
      "text": "most developers don't ever want to have to touch the word prototype, so what we do instead is use a front-end framework like react, view, spelt, angular, and so on."
    },
    {
      "start": 538.0,
      "end": 543.88,
      "text": "all of these Frameworks do the same thing in a slightly different way."
    },
    {
      "start": 541.84,
      "end": 550.44,
      "text": "which is represent the UI as a tree of components."
    },
    {
      "start": 548.68,
      "end": 554.56,
      "text": "a component can encapsulate HTML, CSS, and JavaScript into a format that looks like its own custom HTML element."
    },
    {
      "start": 552.6,
      "end": 557.88,
      "text": "most importantly, they produce declarative code that describes exactly what the UI does."
    },
    {
      "start": 556.36,
      "end": 561.16,
      "text": "and that's much easier to work with than imperative code that you would normally get with just plain vanilla JavaScript."
    },
    {
      "start": 559.52,
      "end": 565.04,
      "text": "at this point, we've taken a look at the front-end stack."
    },
    {
      "start": 562.76,
      "end": 570.2,
      "text": "but now we need to switch gears to the back end starting with node.js, which is a server-side runtime based on JavaScript."
    },
    {
      "start": 570.2,
      "end": 577.52,
      "text": "Node is the most popular because it relies on the same language as the browser."
    },
    {
      "start": 583.88,
      "end": 592.04,
      "text": "In addition, it allows developers to share work remotely thanks to the node package manager."
    },
    {
      "start": 589.96,
      "end": 598.2,
      "text": "A package is also called a module, which is just a file that contains some code with an export statement so it can be used in another file."
    },
    {
      "start": 596.32,
      "end": 604.48,
      "text": "The file can consume a module with an import statement, but now we need to think about how to deliver the actual website from the server to the client."
    },
    {
      "start": 604.48,
      "end": 613.4,
      "text": "The classic option is server-side rendering; in this approach, the client will make a get request for a certain URL."
    },
    {
      "start": 613.4,
      "end": 621.64,
      "text": "Git means you want to retrieve data from a server as opposed to methods like post and patch where the intent is to modify data."
    },
    {
      "start": 621.64,
      "end": 629.96,
      "text": "The server receives the request and then generates all the HTML on the server and sends it back to the client as a response."
    },
    {
      "start": 627.52,
      "end": 636.4,
      "text": "The response contains a status code like 200 for success or levels 400 and 500 for errors."
    },
    {
      "start": 636.4,
      "end": 643.52,
      "text": "If the web page doesn't exist, the server will return a 404 status code, which you've likely seen before as a web user."
    },
    {
      "start": 641.2,
      "end": 647.24,
      "text": "SSR is extremely popular, but in some cases, it may not be fast enough."
    },
    {
      "start": 645.56,
      "end": 653.64,
      "text": "Another approach is the single page application; with this approach, the server only renders a shell for the root URL."
    },
    {
      "start": 651.68,
      "end": 659.32,
      "text": "JavaScript handles the rendering for all other pages on the website; the HTML is generated almost entirely client-side in the browser."
    },
    {
      "start": 659.32,
      "end": 668.08,
      "text": "When the app needs more data, it still makes an HTTP request but only requests a minimal amount of data as JSON."
    },
    {
      "start": 665.76,
      "end": 673.16,
      "text": "JSON is called a data interchange format that can be understood by any programming language."
    },
    {
      "start": 671.88,
      "end": 684.96,
      "text": "This can result in a great user experience; however, it can be very difficult for bots like search engines and social media link previews to understand content on the page."
    },
    {
      "start": 682.96,
      "end": 690.96,
      "text": "This led to another rendering strategy called static site generation."
    },
    {
      "start": 689.08,
      "end": 698.64,
      "text": "In this case, every web page on the site is uploaded to a server in advance, allowing bots to get the information they need, and a frontend JavaScript framework usually takes over to hydrate the HTML to make it fully interactive and behave like a single-page application."
    },
    {
      "start": 697.04,
      "end": 703.76,
      "text": "Performance is extremely important, and you'll want to use tools like Lighthouse to optimize metrics like first contentful paint and time to interactive."
    },
    {
      "start": 701.8,
      "end": 709.96,
      "text": "Now, to implement one of these patterns, most developers will use a full-stack framework like Next.js, Ruby on Rails, Laravel, and so on."
    },
    {
      "start": 707.32,
      "end": 717.76,
      "text": "They abstract away many of the more tedious things developers don't want to deal with, one of which is module bundlers."
    },
    {
      "start": 715.72,
      "end": 723.72,
      "text": "These are tools like Webpack that take all of your JavaScript, CSS, and HTML and package it in a way that can actually work in a browser."
    },
    {
      "start": 722.32,
      "end": 729.08,
      "text": "They might also provide a linter like ESLint to warn you when your code doesn't follow the proper style guidelines."
    },
    {
      "start": 727.64,
      "end": 735.8,
      "text": "Oh, and I almost forgot, you are definitely going to need a database to build a full-stack web application because you need somewhere to store your data, like data about your users."
    },
    {
      "start": 734.44,
      "end": 743.6,
      "text": "But in order to get that data, you'll need to give users a way to log in via a process called user authentication."
    },
    {
      "start": 741.16,
      "end": 751.6,
      "text": "Now, before you deploy your code, you'll need to test it with a web server."
    },
    {
      "start": 748.8,
      "end": 758.64,
      "text": "There are tools like NGINX and Apache to create an HTTP server, but your framework will likely do this for you by serving the files on localhost."
    },
    {
      "start": 756.92,
      "end": 764.8,
      "text": "This makes your own IP address behave like a remote web server."
    },
    {
      "start": 762.92,
      "end": 768.48,
      "text": "When it comes time to deploy, you'll likely use a big cloud provider like AWS."
    },
    {
      "start": 766.88,
      "end": 782.84,
      "text": "There are many tools out there that function as a platform as a service to manage this infrastructure for you in exchange for your money, or if you don't want to get locked in with a giant Tech Corporation, you might host your app on a decentralized blockchain with web 3."
    },
    {
      "start": 781.24,
      "end": 793.68,
      "text": "That's about 1% of what you'll need to know to call yourself a full stack web developer; if that seems overwhelming, don't worry too much, almost nobody knows what the hell they're doing, and we all just use Google to figure things out on the fly."
    },
    {
      "start": 791.36,
      "end": 799.8,
      "text": "Congratulations, you just passed web development 101; thanks for watching, and I will see you in the next one."
    }
  ]
}
```

## 30. Plik: `frontend/src/components/Navbar.js`

```javascript
// frontend/src/components/Navbar.js
import React from 'react';
import './Navbar.css';

function Navbar({ currentView, onNavigateToDashboard }) {
  // Nawigacja dla widoku Dashboard (główna strona)
  const dashboardNavLinks = (
    <>
      <a href="#discover" className="nav-link">discover</a>
      <a href="#dashboard" className="nav-link"><span className="nav-link-my">my</span>dashboard</a>
    </>
  );

  // Nawigacja dla widoku Workspace (strona robocza)
  const workspaceNavLinks = (
    <>
      <a href="#ideas" className="nav-link">Ideas</a>
      <a href="#mydashboard" className="nav-link" onClick={onNavigateToDashboard}>my dashboard</a>
    </>
  );

  return (
    <nav className="main-navbar">
      {/* Możesz tu dodać logo po lewej stronie, jeśli chcesz */}
      {/* <div className="navbar-logo">
        <h1 className="logo-text">AI Buddy</h1>
        <span className="logo-subtext">English</span>
      </div> */}

      <div className="navbar-links">
        {currentView === 'dashboard' ? dashboardNavLinks : workspaceNavLinks}
      </div>
    </nav>
  );
}

export default Navbar;
```

```javascript
import React, { useState, useEffect, useRef } from "react";
import "./NotebookSidebar.css";

const NotebookSidebar = ({
  notebookWords,
  onSpeakWord,
  onDeleteWord,
  onOpenEmailModal,
  onOpenFlashcards,
  onExplainWord,
  activityLog = [],
  onOpenSummary,
  onOpenExercise,
}) => {
  const [activeMenuIndex, setActiveMenuIndex] = useState(null);
  const dropdownRef = useRef(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    const handleOutsideClick = (e) => {
      if (
        dropdownRef.current &&
        !dropdownRef.current.contains(e.target) &&
        !e.target.closest(".menu-trigger-btn")
      ) {
        setActiveMenuIndex(null);
      }
    };
    document.addEventListener("mousedown", handleOutsideClick);
    return () => {
      document.removeEventListener("mousedown", handleOutsideClick);
    };
  }, []);

  return (
    <aside className="notebook-sidebar">
      <div className="sidebar-header">
        <h2>Vocabulary</h2>
        <div className="header-actions">
          <button 
            className="action-icon-btn" 
            onClick={onOpenEmailModal}
            title="Export to Email"
            disabled={notebookWords.length === 0}
          >
            <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="16" height="16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="2" strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round">
              <path d="M4 4h16c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2v12c0 1.1-.9 2-2 2H4c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V6c0-1.1.9-2 2-2z" />
              <polyline points="22,6 12,13 2,6" />
            </svg>
          </button>
          <button 
            className="action-icon-btn practice" 
            onClick={onOpenFlashcards}
            title="Practice Flashcards"
            disabled={notebookWords.length === 0}
          >
            <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="16" height="16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="2" strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round">
              <rect x="3" y="3" width="18" height="18" rx="2" ry="2" />
              <line x1="9" y1="3" x2="9" y2="21" />
            </svg>
          </button>
          <button 
            className="action-icon-btn practice" 
            onClick={onOpenExercise}
            title="Przećwicz słownictwo z tej historii"
            disabled={notebookWords.length === 0}
          >
            <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="16" height="16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="2" strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round">
              <path d="M12 2a3 3 0 0 0-3 3v7a3 3 0 0 0 6 0V5a3 3 0 0 0-3-3z"/>
              <path d="M19 10v2a7 7 0 0 1-14 0v-2M12 19v3M8 22h8"/>
            </svg>
          </button>
          <button 
            className="action-icon-btn summary" 
            onClick={onOpenSummary}
            title="AI Session Summary"
            disabled={activityLog.length === 0}
          >
            <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="16" height="16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="2" strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round">
              <line x1="18" y1="20" x2="18" y2="10" />
              <line x1="12" y1="20" x2="12" y2="4" />
              <line x1="6" y1="20" x2="6" y2="14" />
            </svg>
          </button>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div className="word-count">
        {notebookWords.length} phrase{notebookWords.length === 1 ? "" : "s"} collected
      </div>

      <div className="notebook-scroll-area">
        {notebookWords.length > 0 ? (
          <ul className="notebook-list">
            {notebookWords.map((entry, index) => (
              <li key={index} className="notebook-card">
                <div className="word-content">
                  <span className="original-word">{entry.original}</span>
                  <span className="translated-word">{entry.translated}</span>
                </div>
                <div className="card-actions">
                  <button
                    className="menu-trigger-btn"
                    onClick={() => setActiveMenuIndex(activeMenuIndex === index ? null : index)}
                    title="Options"
                  >
                    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="16" height="16" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="2.5" strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round">
                      <circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1.5" />
                      <circle cx="12" cy="5" r="1.5" />
                      <circle cx="12" cy="19" r="1.5" />
                    </svg>
                  </button>

                  {activeMenuIndex === index && (
                    <div className="card-dropdown-menu" ref={dropdownRef}>
                      <button
                        className="dropdown-item"
                        onClick={() => {
                          onSpeakWord(entry.original);
                          setActiveMenuIndex(null);
                        }}
                      >
                        <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="14" height="14" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="2" strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round" className="dropdown-icon">
                          <polygon points="11 5 6 9 2 9 2 15 6 15 11 19 11 5" />

                      <button

                        }}
                      >

                      </button>
                      <button
                        className="dropdown-item delete"

                          onDeleteWord(entry.original);
                          setActiveMenuIndex(null);
                        }}
                      >
                        <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="14" height="14" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="2" strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round" className="dropdown-icon">
                          <polyline points="3 6 5 6 21 6" />
                          <path d="M19 6v14a2 2 0 0 1-2 2H7a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V6m3 0V4a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h4a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v2" />
                        </svg>
                        Delete
                      </button>
                    </div>
                  )}
                </div>
              </li>
            ))}
          </ul>
        ) : (
          <div className="empty-state">
            <div className="empty-icon">
              <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="32" height="32" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="1.5" strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round">
                <path d="M2 3h6a4 4 0 0 1 4 4v14a3 3 0 0 0-3-3H2z" />
                <path d="M22 3h-6a4 4 0 0 0-4 4v14a3 3 0 0 1 3-3h7z" />
              </svg>
            </div>
            <p>Your notebook is empty.</p>
            <p className="hint">Highlight text in the story to add phrases here.</p>
          </div>
        )}
      </div>
    </aside>
  );
};

export default NotebookSidebar;
```

```javascript
import React, { useState, useRef, useEffect } from "react";
import { API_BASE_URL } from '../../config';
import "./PronunciationPracticeModal.css";

const PronunciationPracticeModal = ({ targetText, user, onClose, onLogActivity, onLogPronunciationError }) => {
  const [isRecording, setIsRecording] = useState(false);
  const [isEvaluating, setIsEvaluating] = useState(false);
  const [evaluation, setEvaluation] = useState(null);
  const [isSpeaking, setIsSpeaking] = useState(false);
  const [recordingSeconds, setRecordingSeconds] = useState(0);

  const mediaRecorderRef = useRef(null);
  const audioChunksRef = useRef([]);
  const recognitionRef = useRef(null);
  const speechTranscriptRef = useRef("");
  const currentAudioRef = useRef(null);
  const timerRef = useRef(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    return () => {
      // Cleanup audio and recognition on unmount
      if (currentAudioRef.current) {
        currentAudioRef.current.pause();
      }
      if (recognitionRef.current) {
        try { recognitionRef.current.stop(); } catch (e) {}
      }
      if (timerRef.current) {
        clearInterval(timerRef.current);
      }
    };
  }, []);

  // Play target text pronunciation using Neural TTS
  const playTargetTTS = async () => {
    if (isSpeaking) {
      if (currentAudioRef.current) {
        currentAudioRef.current.pause();
        setIsSpeaking(false);
      }
      return;
    }

    setIsSpeaking(true);
    try {
      const response = await fetch(`${API_BASE_URL}/api/tts`, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          text: targetText,
          voice: "en-US-BrianNeural"
        })
      });
      if (!response.ok) {
        throw new Error("Failed to fetch TTS audio");
      }
      const data = await response.json();
      if (data.audio_base64) {
        const audioUrl = `data:audio/mp3;base64,${data.audio_base64}`;
        const audio = new Audio(audioUrl);
        
        audio.onended = () => setIsSpeaking(false);
        audio.onerror = () => {
          setIsSpeaking(false);
          alert("Failed to play pronunciation.");
        };

        currentAudioRef.current = audio;
        audio.play();
      } else {
        throw new Error("No audio_base64 in response");
      }
    } catch (err) {
      console.error("Error playing TTS:", err);
      setIsSpeaking(false);
      alert("Failed to play pronunciation.");
    }
  };

  const startRecording = async () => {
    try {
      const stream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({ audio: true });
      mediaRecorderRef.current = new MediaRecorder(stream);
      audioChunksRef.current = [];
      mediaRecorderRef.current.ondataavailable = (e) => {
        if (e.data.size > 0) audioChunksRef.current.push(e.data);
      };

      speechTranscriptRef.current = "";
      const SpeechRecognition = window.SpeechRecognition || window.webkitSpeechRecognition;
      if (SpeechRecognition) {
        const rec = new SpeechRecognition();
        rec.lang = "en-US";
        rec.continuous = false;
        rec.interimResults = false;
        rec.maxAlternatives = 1;

        rec.onresult = (event) => {
          const resultText = event.results[0][0].transcript;
          console.log("Local transcription:", resultText);
          speechTranscriptRef.current = resultText;
        };
        rec.onerror = (e) => {
          console.warn("Local SpeechRecognition error:", e.error);
        };
        recognitionRef.current = rec;
        rec.start();
      }

      mediaRecorderRef.current.onstop = () => {
        const audioBlob = new Blob(audioChunksRef.current, { type: "audio/webm" });
        handleEvaluate(audioBlob, speechTranscriptRef.current);
      };

      mediaRecorderRef.current.start();
      setIsRecording(true);
      setEvaluation(null);
      setRecordingSeconds(0);

      // Start recording timer
      timerRef.current = setInterval(() => {
        setRecordingSeconds((prev) => prev + 1);
      }, 1000);

    } catch (err) {
      console.error(err);
      alert("Dostęp do mikrofonu został zablokowany.");
    }
  };

  const stopRecording = () => {
    if (timerRef.current) {
      clearInterval(timerRef.current);
      timerRef.current = null;
    }
    if (recognitionRef.current) {
      try { recognitionRef.current.stop(); } catch (e) {}
    }
    if (mediaRecorderRef.current && isRecording) {
      mediaRecorderRef.current.stop();
      setIsRecording(false);
      const stream = mediaRecorderRef.current.stream;
      if (stream && typeof stream.getTracks === "function") {
        stream.getTracks().forEach((t) => t.stop());
      }
    }
  };

  const handleEvaluate = async (audioBlob, localTranscript = "") => {
    setIsEvaluating(true);
    setEvaluation(null);

    try {
      const formData = new FormData();
      formData.append("audio", audioBlob, "speech.webm");
      formData.append("target_text", targetText);
      if (localTranscript) {
        formData.append("transcription", localTranscript);
      }

      const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE_URL}/api/mastery-evaluate`, {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { "X-Session-Token": user.token },
        body: formData,
      });

      if (!res.ok) {
        throw new Error("Failed to evaluate pronunciation.");
      }

      const result = await res.json();
      setEvaluation(result);

      // Log practice event to activity log
      if (onLogActivity && result && typeof result.score !== "undefined") {
        onLogActivity({
          type: "practice",
          word_or_phrase: targetText,
          timestamp: Date.now(),
          details: {
            practice_score: result.score,
            practice_sentence: targetText,
            practice_transcription: result.transcription || localTranscript || "",
          },
        });
      }

      // Log specific mispronounced words as pronunciation errors
      if (onLogPronunciationError && result.mispronounced_words && result.mispronounced_words.length > 0) {
        result.mispronounced_words.forEach((word) => {
          onLogPronunciationError(word, targetText);
        });
      }

    } catch (err) {
      console.error("Evaluation error:", err);
      alert("Nie udało się przeanalizować wymowy. Spróbuj ponownie.");
    } finally {
      setIsEvaluating(false);
    }
  };

  const formatTime = (seconds) => {
    const mins = Math.floor(seconds / 60);
    const secs = seconds % 60;
    return `${mins}:${secs < 10 ? "0" : ""}${secs}`;
  };

  return (
    <div className="practice-modal-overlay" data-testid="pronunciation-practice-modal">
      <div className="practice-modal-content glass-panel animate-zoom">
        <header className="practice-modal-header">
          <h3>Przećwicz Wymowę Zdania</h3>
          <button className="close-btn" onClick={onClose} aria-label="Zamknij">&times;</button>
        </header>

        <div className="practice-modal-body">
          <div className="target-text-container">
            <p className="target-label">Zdanie do przeczytania:</p>
            <blockquote className="target-text">"{targetText}"</blockquote>
          </div>

          <div className="practice-actions-row">
            <button 
              className={`btn-tts-listen ${isSpeaking ? "playing" : ""}`}
              onClick={playTargetTTS}
              title="Odsłuchaj poprawną wymowę"
            >
              <span className="btn-icon">
                {isSpeaking ? (
                  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="18" height="18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="2.5" strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round" style={{ display: 'inline-block', verticalAlign: 'middle' }}>
                    <rect x="4" y="4" width="16" height="16" rx="2" ry="2" />
                  </svg>
                ) : (
                  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="18" height="18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="2.5" strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round" style={{ display: 'inline-block', verticalAlign: 'middle' }}>
                    <polygon points="11 5 6 9 2 9 2 15 6 15 11 19 11 5" />
                    <path d="M19.07 4.93a10 10 0 0 1 0 14.14M15.54 8.46a5 5 0 0 1 0 7.07" />
                  </svg>
                )}
              </span>
              {isSpeaking ? "Zatrzymaj" : "Odsłuchaj wzór"}
            </button>

            {isRecording ? (
              <button className="btn-record-voice recording" onClick={stopRecording}>
                <span className="record-pulse-dot"></span>
                Zatrzymaj ({formatTime(recordingSeconds)})
              </button>
            ) : (
              <button className="btn-record-voice" onClick={startRecording} disabled={isEvaluating}>
                <span className="btn-icon">
                  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="18" height="18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth="2.5" strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round" style={{ display: 'inline-block', verticalAlign: 'middle' }}>
                    <path d="M12 1a3 3 0 0 0-3 3v8a3 3 0 0 0 6 0V4a3 3 0 0 0-3-3z" />
                    <path d="M19 10v2a7 7 0 0 1-14 0v-2M12 19v4M8 23h8" />
                  </svg>
                </span>
                Nagraj swój głos
              </button>
            )}
          </div>

          {isEvaluating && (
            <div className="practice-evaluating">
              <div className="spinner"></div>
              <p>Analizowanie Twojej wymowy przez AI...</p>
            </div>
          )}

          {evaluation && (
            <div className="evaluation-results-box animate-zoom">
              <div className="evaluation-score-row">
                <div className={`score-ring ${evaluation.score >= 80 ? "excellent" : evaluation.score >= 60 ? "good" : "needs-practice"}`}>
                  <span className="score-number">{evaluation.score}%</span>
                  <span className="score-label">Wynik</span>
                </div>
                <div className="evaluation-tip-box">
                  <h4>Analiza Wymowy:</h4>
                  <p className="evaluation-tip">{evaluation.tip}</p>
                </div>
              </div>

              {evaluation.transcription && (
                <div className="evaluation-detail-section">
                  <strong>Twoja wymowa (tekst):</strong>
                  <p className="transcription-text">"{evaluation.transcription}"</p>
                </div>
              )}

              {evaluation.corrections && evaluation.corrections !== "Brak błędów" && (
                <div className="evaluation-detail-section corrections">
                  <strong>Wykryte błędy / luki:</strong>
                  <p className="corrections-text">{evaluation.corrections}</p>
                  {evaluation.mispronounced_words && evaluation.mispronounced_words.length > 0 && (
                    <div className="mispronounced-chips">
                      {evaluation.mispronounced_words.map((word, idx) => (
                        <span key={idx} className="mispronounced-chip">
                          ⚠️ {word}
                        </span>
                      ))}
                    </div>
                  )}
                </div>
              )}

              {evaluation.corrections === "Brak błędów" && (
                <div className="evaluation-detail-section perfect">
                  <p className="perfect-text">🎉 Idealna wymowa! Brak wykrytych błędów.</p>
                </div>
              )}
            </div>
          )}
        </div>

        <footer className="practice-modal-footer">
          <button className="btn-close-footer" onClick={onClose}>Zamknij</button>
        </footer>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
};

export default PronunciationPracticeModal;
```
